page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.20xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance from the High Clock Speed instance family, provisioned under the KVM hypervisor. The instance is equipped with 80 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Paired with this processing core count is 768.0 GB of memory, which provides an allocation ratio of 9.6 GB of RAM per vCPU. This high memory-to-core balance positions the instance specifically for compute tasks requiring significant working memory sets.

In terms of I/O infrastructure, the ecs.hfr6.20xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node data transfer across cloud environments. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage, which necessitates reliance on remote cloud block storage for persistent data. Furthermore, the configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators, focusing hardware resources purely on CPU and host memory operations.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, this configuration aggregates large memory capacity and dedicated high-frequency cores into a single virtual machine. This reduces operational overhead relative to maintaining distributed clusters for equivalent memory footprints. The server type is suitable for workloads such as in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, transactional databases, and memory-bound enterprise software suites.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.20xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance tailored for resource-intensive workloads requiring both substantial core counts and high memory capacity. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, it features 80 dedicated vCPUs driven by 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processors. The system delivers 768 GB of system memory, establishing a generous allocation of 9.6 GB per vCPU that prevents memory bottlenecks in large-footprint applications. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth interface. The instance includes no local storage, relying entirely on network-attached block storage options, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. With its combination of sustained compute capability and elevated memory density, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for enterprise-grade workloads without requiring multi-socket bare-metal provisioning. It is well matched for in-memory databases, large scale caching layers, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
